To make an informed decision over which message you would like to send, we describe Stage 3 now:

In Stage 3, you will decide in the role of participant A. The other participant will also decide in the role of participant A. At the end of Stage 3, a random draw with equal chance determines if you are in the role of participant A or B (think of this as a coin flip). If you are participant A, your decision will determine the payoff. If you are participant B, the decision of the other participant in the role of participant A will determine the payoff.

Participant A will decide whether they wish to roll or to not roll a die. If participant A chooses Don’t Roll, participant A receives 14 points and participant B receives 0 points. If participant A chooses Roll, participant A receives 10 points. The computer will simulate the roll of a six-sided die. Thus, it will draw a random integer between 1 and 6, where every integer has the same chance of being drawn. The result of this die roll determines participant B’s payoff. If the number 1 is rolled, participant B receives 0 points. If one of the numbers 2–6 is rolled, participant B receives 12 points.

This information is summarised in the following table:

In case A chooses ... ... A receives ... ... and B receives ...
... Don't Roll ... ... 14 points ... ... 0 points ...
... Roll and the die returns 1 ... ... 10 points ... ... 0 points ...
... Roll and the die returns 2,3,4,5 or 6 ... ... 10 points ... ... 12 points.

Information on the die rolling decisions: If you are in the role of participant A, you will learn the payoff of both participants at the end. In case you have chosen to Roll, you will also find out the number that was rolled.

If you are in the role of participant B, you will learn only your own payoff. Other than what can be concluded from this payoff, participant B will not find out which choice participant A has made.
